text.p: Germany's Mannesmann AG said on Thursday it had finalised a deal with U.S. communications giant AT&T Corp and Europe's Unisource group to form a new phone company with German railways Deutsche Bahn AG.

The Mannesmann-led consortium has taken a 49.8 percent stake in Deutsche Bahn's communications subsidiary DBKom GmbH, merged it with its own CNI corporate communications unit and renamed the group Mannesmann Arcor AG & Co.

Arcor combines the strengths of international activities of AT&T/Unisource, Mannesmann's experience in operating Germany's leading cellular phone network and the railway's communications network to form a potent competitor to Deutsche Telekom AG.

"The goal of Arcor, the new telephone company, is to remain the second largest provider of fixed-wire telecommunications services after Deutsche Telekom," said Arcor chairman and Mannesmann board member Peter Mihatsch.

Arcor currently focuses on providing communications services to German businesses. It owns and operates a 40,000 km (24,850 miles) national communications network along the railway lines, of which 5,000 km (3,107 miles) is high-speed optical fibre. It has around 300,000 telephone connections.

It is upgrading and expanding the network and plans to have completed installation of a national fibre-optic backbone network by the middle of this year. It already operates the second largest high-speed digital ISDN network after recently- listed Deutsche Telekom.
The groundwork for Arcor was laid last July, when Deutsche Bahn AG picked the Mannesmann-led consortium as the winner in a bid for nearly half of the railway's internal telecoms business.
Mannesmann holds 60 percent of the consortium, while AT&T and Unisource each hold 15 percent. Germany's largest bank Deutsche Bank AG holds the remaining 10 percent.
Unisource is a business communications services alliance equally owned by PTT Telecom Nederlands, Swiss Telecom PTT, Telia of Sweden and Spain's Telefonica.
Deutsche Bahn currently holds 50.2 percent of Arcor, but the Mannesmann consortium has the option to raise its stake to 74.9 percent.
"I am very certain that we will do this in 1999," said Mihatsch.
Arcor plans to invest 800 million marks ($488.2 million) this year and a total of up to four billion marks over the next five years. It plans to break even by the year 2000.

DBKom and CNI combined invested a total of 400 million marks in 1996 and achieved turnover of some 900 million marks. Arcor sales are expected to reach more than one billion marks this year, Mihatsch said.
Volker Ruloff, Arcor finance chief, dismissed speculation that the company could be floated on the stock exchange, saying: "We do not intend to take the company public."
But Mihatsch said that there was always the possibility that more partners could be brought on board if someone makes the right offer and brought value to the group. ($1=1.6383 Mark)
